summary.title: Introduction to Scrum for Managers and Executives
summary.one_liner: A slide deck explaining the core Scrum roles, events and rules (sprints, product backlog, team size) and reporting survey results on how teams compared Scrum with their previous approach.
takeaways: Scrum uses fixed-length sprints (typically 1-4 weeks) with a committed scope that does not change mid-sprint.
The Product Owner owns a single prioritized Product Backlog based on business value and risk.
Scrum teams are cross-functional, self-organizing, and ideally about 7 people +/- 2.

Yahoo! survey data (first 80 teams, 18 months after adoption) reported a 36% average productivity increase and higher reported morale, accountability and collaboration compared with the previous approach.
summary.summary: This slide deck from goodagile, a Scrum training and consulting firm, introduces Scrum to managers and executives. It opens with common problems companies face (long time-to-market, high project failure, low morale) and lists companies and project types where Scrum is used. It then presents Yahoo! survey results comparing Scrum with previous approaches on productivity, morale, accountability, collaboration and quality. The last sections explain the basics of Scrum: roles, the product backlog, team structure, sprint rules and sprint planning.
